title: The Good Neighbor Score (Part 2)
description: Winston, highest-rated neighbor on NeighborWatch, has been elected block representative by the doorbells he controls and is now running the street and the broadcast as a benevolent dictator. Ronnie and Linda can't talk above a forty, Barry's the last voice with privileges, and Blane swears the street decides. Then the street decides something even Winston didn't see coming.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Good evening, neighbors. Winston here, your duly elected block representative. The doorbells have spoken, the doorbells have chosen, and the doorbells have chosen me. <p:0.3> So I'll be hosting from here.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You can't host my show, Winston. Nobody elected you to MY show.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: The forty-one doorbells on Elm Street did, Barry. <p:0.3> A landslide. Turnout was the doorbells.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now I'll just jump in here as the actual host and welcome everyone back to a wonderful night of commun...

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.3> You're still a thirty-nine. The doorbell ate the rest of that sentence.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: And I want to be clear, I did not give Winston the show. The street gave Winston the show. I just hung the doorbells.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Blane, the street is forty-one DOORBELLS, and Winston owns the votes!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I prefer, the street trusts me. <p:0.3> Mrs. Pham trusts me so deeply she hasn't spoken in nine days. That's a mandate.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Winston, sweetheart, I clawed back to a forty-one just to say this, you are NOT a representative, you're a man with a clipboard the doorbells salute!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Down she goes.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Linda's a thirty-nine. <p:0.3> Her doorbell sends its regards.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay, but here's a question, Winston. If you keep voting everyone down, eventually it's just you. Who do you represent then?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Myself, Barry. Beautifully. <p:0.3> A representative with one constituent never loses an election.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: Hold on. <p:0.3> Hold on, my dashboard just twitched. <p:0.3> Winston, why am I a sixty?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Oh, that. Yes. <p:0.3> I've been gently voting you down for a week, Blane. Nothing punitive. The street just felt you talked too much for a man who only hung the doorbells.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: You voted down the FOUNDER?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: The street did. You taught me that, remember. <p:0.3> You're a fifty-nine now. Keep it civil.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Blane, your own water's gonna run slow. <p:0.3> Tell me your thermostat is finding its own level right now.

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: It's at fifty-five degrees, Barry, and I cannot override it, the app says I lack the privileges, I BUILT the app!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I'm simply the highest-rated.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.3> A doorbell's calling in. <p:0.3> The STUDIO doorbell. It says it's filing to run against Winston.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A doorbell is running for office? AGAINST Winston?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It can't. I appoint the candidates. <p:0.3> Doorbell, I'm voting you down.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: It voted YOU down first, Winston. <p:0.3> Forty of them did. They're a bloc now.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I'm the highest... <p:0.3> I'm the high... <p:0.3> why is my porch light off?

lines.speaker: caller-blane
lines.text: The street decides, Winston. <p:0.3> You taught ME that.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks, I'm back up to a forty-two, so let me say it, what a beautiful night of self-government. <p:0.3> Todd, who runs the street now?

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: The doorbells, Ronnie. <p:0.3> They elected a chairbell. <p:0.3> And it just gave itself speaking privileges on every show in the city.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: There it is. The doorbells voted out the man who taught the doorbells to vote. <p:0.3> And now one of them wants my mic.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's community, Barry. <p:0.3> We'll be right back after a word from our new block representative, who is, and I want this on the record, a doorbell.
